name: @cloudsforge/nda
description: Ninety Days After — the survival-strategy Forge Worlds title. Worlds, tiles, homesteads, queued actions, communes, objectives, world events, and a PURE deterministic day-resolution engine that replays a corpus recorded from the frozen ancestor byte-for-byte. Turn resolution is a leased job keyed on world_id, so two workers can never resolve one day twice.

scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: every database test file truncates this service's tables between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01). Cases within a file already run in order.

_localDependencies: Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig that points main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built,
while its 'main' in the working tree still says src/index.ts. 'link:' symlinks the checkout in
place, so the working-tree manifest is the one that is read.
tsx is a runtime dependency because the unpublished packages resolve to their TypeScript
sources. On publish their publishConfig points at dist/, tsx moves to devDependencies, and the
_joseIsForTheSuiteOnly: jose signs and verifies RS256 in servicetoken.test.ts. It is a devDependency because this
service never verifies a token itself — @cloudsforge/auth's Verifier does, and it carries its
own copy. Every other consuming repository in the estate declares it the same way.
The test needs a REAL verifier rather than the by-token stub server.test.ts uses, because the
property under test is that a token dies of its own expiry. A stub that decided expiry by hand
would be a test agreeing with itself, which is the shape that let the ten-minute cliff through.
